newsitem.title: SUDAN: U.N. in talks with Sudan over detained plane.
newsitem.headline: U.N. in talks with Sudan over detained plane.

text.p: The United Nations is negotiating with Sudanese officials in Khartoum over the fate of one of its chartered planes which security officials detained two days ago, a privately-owned newspaper said on Tuesday.
Sudan said on Sunday it had grounded a relief plane it said was masquerading as a supply aircraft for the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA).
Army spokesman Mohammed el-Senoussi told state radio Omdurman at the time that officials grounded the plane after it landed without a permit at the airport in Bor town in the southern Jonglei state.

Al-Alwan daily newspaper on Tuesday quoted government sources as saying the plane was chartered by the United Nations Children's Fund as part of the U.N.-sponsored relief operation named Operation Lifeline Sudan.

Senoussi said on Sunday the state had evidence the plane was serving the rebel SPLA which has been fighting for autonomy of the mostly Christian and animist south from the Islamist Arabised north for the past 13 years.
Security officials say the pilot had in his permission documents intended to assist the SPLA.
Operation Lifeline Sudan brings together the U.N. and other specialised agencies and voluntary organisations to take food to people affected by the civil war in the south of the country.
